blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: A pricing service, compiled for Java 17, formats each quote with `return currency + " " + amount + " valid until " + expiry;`. A colleague wants to rewrite it with a `StringBuilder` to avoid the cost of the three `+`. What does `javap -c` show for the method as written?

options.text: One `invokedynamic` call in total, since javac compiles the whole expression into a single concatenation
options.says: since Java 9 one expression is one invokedynamic to StringConcatFactory, which sizes and fills the result once

options.text: One `invokedynamic` call per `+`, since each `+` that takes a variable is linked as a concatenation of its own
options.says: the javap output of a five-+ line showed one invokedynamic

options.text: One `StringBuilder` with an `append` per operand, since javac has translated `+` into such a chain all along
options.says: that was the translation up to Java 8, or with --release 8; Java 17 class files hold one invokedynamic

options.text: One new `StringBuilder` per `+`, since each `+` that takes a variable gets a builder and a `toString` of its own
options.says: neither translation ever made one builder per +; since Java 9 there is one invokedynamic

origin.section: One `+` Expression Is One Concatenation, Compiled to a Single Call

questions.stem: A job builds an email digest with `body += renderRow(r);` inside a loop over the rows. Last month, with 30,000 rows, the loop allocated about 6 GB. This month has 60,000 rows of the same size. About how much will the loop allocate?

options.text: About 12 GB, since each pass makes one new String about as long as the row it adds
options.says: each pass's new String holds everything built so far, not only the new row

options.text: About 24 GB, since each pass makes one new String about as long as everything built so far
options.says: allocation grows with the square of the row count: twice the rows, four times the bytes

options.text: About 6 GB, since after warm-up the JIT turns the repeated `+=` into one growing buffer
options.says: the measured runs were after warm-up, and the allocation still quadrupled when the rows doubled

options.text: About 6 GB, since javac compiles the loop's repeated `+=` into one `invokedynamic` call
options.says: one invokedynamic covers one expression; the loop runs it once per row, each time with the whole text so far as an argument

origin.section: `+=` in a Loop Copies Everything Built So Far, on Every Pass

questions.stem: Each night a job posts `failed.stream().collect(Collectors.joining(", ", "Failed jobs: ", ""))` to the team channel. What text does it post on a night when `failed` is an empty list?

options.text: The prefix and nothing after it, since the prefix and the suffix are written even when there are no elements
options.says: joining writes prefix + suffix for an empty stream, as the Low stock: . run showed

options.text: Nothing at all, an empty string, since the prefix and the suffix are written only around at least one element
options.says: the run showed Low stock: . for an empty list: prefix and suffix are always written

options.text: The prefix and then null, since an empty stream gives the joiner one null element to convert after the prefix
options.says: an empty stream has no elements at all, so nothing is converted; the joiner writes prefix + suffix

options.text: Nothing at all but null, since an empty stream gives the joiner one null result to return in place of the prefix
options.says: joining never returns null or the text null for an empty stream; it writes prefix + suffix

origin.section: Repeated Text Goes into One Buffer, and a Joiner Places the Separators

questions.stem: A notification service builds an email subject with `"Order ".concat(ref)`, and a colleague's branch builds it with `"Order " + ref`. What do the two versions do for an order whose `ref` was never set and is `null`?

options.text: `+` gives `Order null` and `concat` throws, since `+` turns a null reference into the text null and `concat` does not
options.says: + applies string conversion, so null becomes the text null, while concat(null) throws NullPointerException

options.text: `+` gives `Order ` and `concat` throws, since `+` leaves out a null operand and `concat` does not
options.says: + never leaves an operand out: null becomes the four letters null

options.text: Both give `Order null`, since `concat` turns a null reference into the text null just as `+` does
Both give `Order `, since `concat` leaves out a null argument just as `+` leaves out a null operand

origin.section: `+` Turns Every Operand into Text, and null Becomes the Word "null"

concepts: Since Java 9 one concatenation expression compiles to a single invokedynamic call that sizes the result once, so rewriting it as a StringBuilder chain gains nothing.
